avoid_supplements.name: Morphine/Opioid supplements or concurrent use
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive CNS depression and respiratory depression risk; gabapentin increases opioid bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or require dose adjustment and enhanced monitoring for respiratory depression

caution_supplements.name: Valerian root
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased sedation or dizziness

caution_supplements.name: Kava kava
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor for excessive sedation

caution_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential for CNS effects; may reduce gabapentin efficacy in some contexts
caution_supplements.action: Monitor clinical response and CNS symptoms

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May decrease gabapentin absorption rate; food delays but does not significantly reduce overall bioavailability
caution_foods.action: Take gabapentin consistently with or without food; maintain routine for consistency

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS depression effects; increased risk of sedation, dizziness, impaired cognition
caution_foods.action: Limit or avoid alcohol consumption; counsel on CNS depression risks

monitoring_notes: Gabapentin undergoes minimal metabolism and has no significant CYP450 interactions, making it relatively safe from drug-drug interactions at the metabolic level. Primary concerns involve additive CNS depression with opioids, other CNS depressants, and alcohol; monitor renal function as gabapentin is renally cleared and may accumulate in renal impairment.
